metadata.title: On the existence of asymptotically good linear codes in minor-closed classes
metadata.authors: Peter Nelson, Stefan H.M. van Zwam

nodes.name: Code parameters and the prime subfield $\Fprime$
nodes.statement: For a finite field $\bF$, let $\Fprime$ denote the unique subfield of $\bF$ of prime order. For a linear code $C$, denote the length of $C$ by $n_C$, the dimension of $C$ by $k_C$, and the minimum Hamming distance of $C$ by $d_C$. In short, $C$ is an $[n_C, k_C, d_C]$ code.
nodes.statement_short: Notation: $\Fprime$ is the prime subfield of $\bF$, and $[n_C,k_C,d_C]$ are length, dimension and minimum distance of a code $C$.
differentia: of prime order

nodes.name: Asymptotically good class of codes
nodes.statement: A class $\cC$ of codes is \emph{asymptotically good} if there exists $\varepsilon > 0$ such that for every $n \in \bZ^+$ there is a code $C \in \cC$ of length $n_C \geq n$ satisfying $k_C \ge \varepsilon n_C$ and $d_C \ge \varepsilon n_C$.
nodes.statement_short: A class of codes is asymptotically good if it contains codes of unbounded length with rate and relative distance both bounded below by a fixed $\varepsilon > 0$.
differentia: there exists $\varepsilon > 0$ such that for every $n \in \bZ^+$ there is a code $C \in \cC$ of length $n_C \geq n$ satisfying $k_C \ge \varepsilon n_C$ and $d_C \ge \varepsilon n_C$

nodes.name: Puncturing of a code
nodes.statement: Given a code $C$, the \emph{puncturing} of $C$ at $i$ is the code obtained from $C$ by removing the $i$th coordinate from each word.
differentia: by removing the $i$th coordinate from each word

nodes.name: Shortening of a code
nodes.statement: The \emph{shortening} of $C$ at $i$ is the code obtained from $C$ by selecting only the codewords of $C$ having a $0$ in position $i$, and then puncturing the resulting code at $i$.
differentia: by selecting only the codewords of $C$ having a $0$ in position $i$
and then puncturing the resulting code at $i$

nodes.name: $\bF$-represented matroid
nodes.statement: If $\bF$ is a field, then an \emph{$\bF$-represented matroid} is a pair $M = (E,U)$, where $E$ is a finite set and $U$ is a subspace of $\bF^E$. We often omit `$\bF$-represented' when the context is clear. We write $|M|$ for $|E|$.
nodes.statement_short: An $\bF$-represented matroid is a finite ground set $E$ together with a subspace $U \subseteq \bF^E$ (i.e. exactly a linear code).
differentia: $E$ is a finite set
$U$ is a subspace of $\bF^E$

nodes.name: Generator matrix of a represented matroid
nodes.statement: If $A$ is an $\bF$-matrix with column set $E$ such that $\rowspace(A) = U$, then we write $M = M(A)$; we call $A$ a \emph{generator matrix} for $M$ and say that $A$ \emph{generates} $M$.
differentia: $\rowspace(A) = U$

nodes.name: Rank function $r_M$
nodes.statement: For $X \subseteq E$ we write $u|X$ for the restriction of the vector $u$ to those coordinates indexed by $X$, we write $U|X$ for the space $\{u|X: u \in U\}$, and we write $r_M(X)$ for the dimension of $U|X$. We denote $r_M(E)$ simply by $r(M)$. We call $r_M$ the \emph{rank function} of $M$.
nodes.statement_short: $r_M(X)$ is the dimension of the projection $U|X$; $r(M) = r_M(E)$.
differentia: $r_M(X)$ is the dimension of $U|X$

nodes.name: Projectively equivalent represented matroids
nodes.statement: If $A_2$ is an $\bF$-matrix obtained from an $\bF$-matrix $A_1$ by nonzero column scalings, then $M(A_1)$ and $M(A_2)$ are formally distinct but share the same rank function. We give a name to this equivalence: two $\bF$-represented matroids $(E,U_1)$ and $(E,U_2)$ are \emph{projectively equivalent} if $U_2 = \{uD: u \in U_1\}$ for some nonsingular diagonal matrix $D$.
nodes.statement_short: Two represented matroids are projectively equivalent when one subspace is obtained from the other by a nonsingular diagonal (column-scaling) transformation.
differentia: $U_2 = \{uD: u \in U_1\}$ for some nonsingular diagonal matrix $D$

nodes.name: Dual matroid $M^*$
nodes.statement: The \emph{dual matroid} $M^*$ of an $\bF$-represented matroid $M = (E,U)$ is defined to be $(E,U^{\perp})$, where $U^\perp$ denotes the orthogonal complement of $U$.
differentia: equal to $(E,U^{\perp})$, where $U^\perp$ denotes the orthogonal complement of $U$

nodes.name: Deletion and contraction
nodes.statement: For $X \subseteq E$ we write $M \del X$ for $(E-X,U|(E-X))$ and $M \con X$ for $(M^* \del X)^*$; these are the matroids obtained from $M$ by \emph{deletion} and \emph{contraction} of $X$ respectively; these operations correspond to puncturing and shortening of codes.
nodes.statement_short: Deletion restricts the subspace to $E-X$ and contraction is its dual operation; they correspond to puncturing and shortening of codes.
differentia: $M \del X$ is $(E-X,U|(E-X))$
$M \con X$ is $(M^* \del X)^*$

nodes.name: Minor of a represented matroid
nodes.statement: If $N$ is an $\bF$-represented matroid that is projectively equivalent to $M \con C \del D$ for some disjoint subsets $C$ and $D$ of $E$, then we say $N$ is a \emph{minor} of $M$.
differentia: projectively equivalent to $M \con C \del D$ for some disjoint subsets $C$ and $D$ of $E$

nodes.name: Minor-closed class of matroids
nodes.statement: A class $\cM$ of matroids is \emph{minor-closed} if $\cM$ is closed under taking minors and isomorphism.
differentia: closed under taking minors and isomorphism

nodes.name: Spanning, independent and dependent sets
nodes.statement: A set $X \subseteq E$ is \emph{spanning} in $M$ if $r_M(X) = r(M)$ and \emph{independent} in $M$ if $r_M(X) = |X|$. If $X$ is not independent then $X$ is \emph{dependent}.
differentia: spanning if $r_M(X) = r(M)$
independent if $r_M(X) = |X|$
dependent if not independent

nodes.name: Circuit and cocircuit
nodes.statement: A \emph{circuit} of $M$ is a minimal dependent set and a \emph{cocircuit} of $M$ is a minimal dependent set of $M^*$, or equivalently a minimal set $C$ satisfying $r(M \del C) < r(M)$.
differentia: a circuit is minimal dependent in $M$
a cocircuit is minimal dependent in $M^*$, equivalently a minimal set $C$ satisfying $r(M \del C) < r(M)$

nodes.name: Girth $g(M)$
nodes.statement: For a matroid $M$, we write $g(M)$ for the size of a smallest circuit of $M$, also called the \emph{girth} of $M$.
nodes.genus: size of a smallest circuit of $M$

nodes.name: Vertically $t$-connected matroid
nodes.statement: for $t \in \bZ^+$, a matroid $M = (E,U)$ is \emph{vertically $t$-connected} if, for every partition $(A,B)$ of $E$ satisfying $r_M(A) + r_M(B) < r(M) + t - 1$, either $A$ or $B$ is spanning in $M$.
nodes.statement_short: Vertical $t$-connectivity: no partition of $E$ with small combined rank has both sides non-spanning.
differentia: for every partition $(A,B)$ of $E$ satisfying $r_M(A) + r_M(B) < r(M) + t - 1$, either $A$ or $B$ is spanning in $M$

nodes.name: $\bF$-frame matrix and $\bF$-represented frame matroid
nodes.statement: An \emph{$\bF$-frame matrix} is an $\bF$-matrix in which every column has at most two nonzero entries, and an \emph{$\bF$-represented frame matroid} is a matroid having an $\bF$-frame matrix as a generator matrix.
differentia: every column has at most two nonzero entries
has an $\bF$-frame matrix as a generator matrix

nodes.name: $\Gamma$-labelled digraph
nodes.statement: For a group $\Gamma$, a \emph{$\Gamma$-labelled digraph} is a pair $(G,\Sigma)$, where $G = (V,E)$ is a directed graph (allowing loops and multiple edges) and $\Sigma: E \to \Gamma$ is an assignment of a label in $\Gamma$ to every arc of $G$.
differentia: $G = (V,E)$ is a directed graph (allowing loops and multiple edges)
$\Sigma: E \to \Gamma$ is an assignment of a label in $\Gamma$ to every arc of $G$

nodes.name: Graph representation of an $\bF$-frame matrix
nodes.statement: If $A$ is an $\bF$-frame matrix with row set $V$ and column set $E$, then a \emph{graph representation} of $A$ is an $\bF^{\times}$-labelled digraph $(G,\Sigma)$, where $G = (V,E)$ and $(G,\Sigma)$ satisfies the following conditions: \begin{itemize} \item If $A[e]$ has two nonzero entries in rows $x$ and $y$, then $e$ is an arc of $G$ from $x$ to $y$ with label $-A[e,x]A[e,y]^{-1}$ or an arc of $G$ from $y$ to $x$ with label $-A[e,y]A[e,x]^{-1}$, and \item If $A[e]$ has exactly one nonzero entry, then $e$ is a loop of $G$ at $x$ with arbitrary label in $\bF^\times - \{1\}$. \item If $A[e] = 0$, then $e$ is a loop of $G$ with label $1$. \end{itemize}
nodes.statement_short: A graph representation encodes each column of a frame matrix as an arc (or loop) of an $\bF^{\times}$-labelled digraph on the row set, with label determined by the ratio of the two nonzero entries.
differentia: each column with two nonzero entries in rows $x$ and $y$ becomes an arc with label $-A[e,x]A[e,y]^{-1}$ or $-A[e,y]A[e,x]^{-1}$
each column with exactly one nonzero entry becomes a loop with arbitrary label in $\bF^\times - \{1\}$
each zero column becomes a loop with label $1$

nodes.name: Sign of a cycle and balanced cycle
nodes.statement: A \emph{cycle} or \emph{path} of a digraph $G$ will denote any cycle or path of the underlying undirected graph of $G$. Let $C$ be a cycle of $G$, and $v_1,e_1,v_2,e_2,\dotsc,e_{k-1},v_k=v_1$ be a corresponding alternating sequence of vertices and arcs of $G$ (there are two choices for this sequence). Let $C^+$ be the set of $e_i$ such that $e_i$ is directed from $v_i$ to $v_{i+1}$ in $G$, and $C^-$ be the set of all other $e_i$. The \emph{sign} of $C$ (relative to this sequence) is $\prod_{e \in C^+} \Sigma(e) \prod_{e\in C^-} \Sigma(e)^{-1}$. We say that $C$ is a \emph{balanced} cycle of $(G,\Sigma)$ if $\sign(C) = 1$. Note that a cycle being balanced does not depend on the choice of sequence of vertices and edges.
nodes.statement_short: The sign of a cycle is the alternating product of its arc labels, and a cycle is balanced when its sign is $1$.
differentia: sign is $\prod_{e \in C^+} \Sigma(e) \prod_{e\in C^-} \Sigma(e)^{-1}$
balanced if $\sign(C) = 1$

nodes.name: Resigning a labelled digraph
nodes.statement: We say $(G, \Sigma')$ was obtained from $(G, \Sigma)$ by \emph{resigning} if, for some $\gamma \in \Gamma$ and for some partition $(U,W)$ of the vertices of $G$, we have \begin{align*} \Sigma'(e) = \begin{cases} \gamma \Sigma(e) & \text{ if } e \text{ runs from } U \text{ to } W;\\ \gamma^{-1} \Sigma(e) & \text{ if } e \text{ runs from } W \text{ to } U;\\ \Sigma(e) & \text{ otherwise}. \end{cases} \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Resigning multiplies the labels of arcs crossing a vertex partition by $\gamma$ (or $\gamma^{-1}$), leaving other labels fixed.
differentia: for some $\gamma \in \Gamma$ and some partition $(U,W)$ of the vertices of $G$, labels of arcs from $U$ to $W$ are multiplied by $\gamma$, labels of arcs from $W$ to $U$ by $\gamma^{-1}$, and all others are unchanged

nodes.name: $(\alpha,\beta)$-good sequence of matroids
nodes.statement: For $\alpha,\beta \in \bR$ we say a sequence $M_0,M_1 \dotsc,$ of matroids is \emph{$(\alpha,\beta)$-good} if $|M_i| \ge i$, $r(M_i) \ge \alpha |M_i|$ and $g(M_i^*) \ge \beta|M_i|$ for each $i \in \bZ_0^+$.
nodes.statement_short: A matroid sequence is $(\alpha,\beta)$-good when sizes grow, ranks are at least $\alpha|M_i|$ and cogirths at least $\beta|M_i|$.
differentia: $|M_i| \ge i$
$r(M_i) \ge \alpha |M_i|$
$g(M_i^*) \ge \beta|M_i|$ for each $i \in \bZ_0^+$

nodes.name: Asymptotically good class of matroids
nodes.statement: A class $\cM$ of matroids is \emph{asymptotically good} if $\cM$ contains an $(\alpha,\beta)$-good sequence for some $\alpha,\beta \in \bR^+$.
differentia: contains an $(\alpha,\beta)$-good sequence for some $\alpha,\beta \in \bR^+$

nodes.name: Elementary projection and elementary lift
nodes.statement: If $M_1 = (E,U_1)$ and $M_2 = (E,U_2)$ are $\bF$-represented matroids and there is an $\bF$-represented matroid $M$ with ground set $E \cup \{e\}$ satisfying $M \del e = M_1$ and $M \con e = M_2$, then we say that $M_2$ is an \emph{elementary projection} of $M_1$ and $M_1$ is an \emph{elementary lift} of $M_2$.
nodes.statement_short: $M_2$ is an elementary projection of $M_1$ when both arise from one matroid on $E \cup \{e\}$ by deleting, resp. contracting, the single element $e$.
nodes.genus: relation between $\bF$-represented matroids $M_1$ and $M_2$ on ground set $E$
differentia: there is an $\bF$-represented matroid $M$ with ground set $E \cup \{e\}$ satisfying $M \del e = M_1$ and $M \con e = M_2$

nodes.name: Perturbation distance $\dist(M_1,M_2)$
nodes.statement: For arbitrary $\bF$-represented matroids $M_1$ and $M_2$ on a common ground set $E$, we write $\dist(M_1,M_2)$ for the minimum number of elementary lifts/projections required to transform $M_1$ into $M_2$.
differentia: required to transform $M_1$ into $M_2$

nodes.name: Theorem 1.1 (main theorem)
nodes.statement: Let $\bF$ be a finite field. If $\cC$ is an asymptotically good class of linear codes over $\bF$, then every linear code $C'$ over $\Fprime$ can be obtained from a code $C \in \cC$ by a sequence of puncturings and shortenings.
nodes.statement_short: An asymptotically good class of $\bF$-linear codes must yield, by puncturing and shortening, every linear code over the prime subfield $\Fprime$.
assumptions: Let $\bF$ be a finite field.
If $\cC$ is an asymptotically good class of linear codes over $\bF$
conclusions: then every linear code $C'$ over $\Fprime$ can be obtained from a code $C \in \cC$ by a sequence of puncturings and shortenings.

nodes.name: Theorem 1.2 (prime-field restatement)
nodes.statement: Let $\bF$ be a field of prime order. If $\cC$ is a proper subclass of the linear codes over $\bF$ that is closed under puncturing and shortening, then $\cC$ is not asymptotically good.
nodes.statement_short: Over a prime field, every proper puncturing/shortening-closed class of linear codes fails to be asymptotically good.
assumptions: Let $\bF$ be a field of prime order.
If $\cC$ is a proper subclass of the linear codes over $\bF$ that is closed under puncturing and shortening
conclusions: then $\cC$ is not asymptotically good.

nodes.name: Structure theorem for highly connected matroids in minor-closed classes
nodes.statement: Let $\bF$ be a finite field and let $\cM$ be a minor-closed class of $\bF$-represented matroids not containing all projective geometries over $\Fprime$. There exists $k \in \bZ^+$ such that every vertically $k$-connected matroid $M$ in $\cM$ satisfies $\dist(M,N) \le k$ or $\dist(M^*,N) \le k$ for some $\bF$-represented frame matroid $N$.
nodes.statement_short: In a minor-closed class missing some $\Fprime$-projective geometry, every highly vertically connected member is a bounded perturbation of a frame matroid or of the dual of one.
nodes.origin_citation: Geelen, Gerards & Whittle, arXiv:1312.5012 (Lemma 2.1 and Theorems 3.2, 3.3)
assumptions: Let $\bF$ be a finite field
let $\cM$ be a minor-closed class of $\bF$-represented matroids not containing all projective geometries over $\Fprime$
conclusions: There exists $k \in \bZ^+$ such that every vertically $k$-connected matroid $M$ in $\cM$ satisfies $\dist(M,N) \le k$ or $\dist(M^*,N) \le k$ for some $\bF$-represented frame matroid $N$.

nodes.name: Theorem 6.1 (asymptotic goodness iff all projective geometries)
nodes.statement: Let $\bF$ be a finite field. If $\cM$ is a minor-closed class of $\bF$-represented matroids, then $\cM$ is asymptotically good if and only if $\cM$ contains all projective geometries over $\Fprime$.
nodes.statement_short: A minor-closed class of $\bF$-represented matroids is asymptotically good exactly when it contains every projective geometry over $\Fprime$.
assumptions: Let $\bF$ be a finite field.
If $\cM$ is a minor-closed class of $\bF$-represented matroids
conclusions: then $\cM$ is asymptotically good if and only if $\cM$ contains all projective geometries over $\Fprime$.

nodes.name: Proposition 2.1 (existence of a graph representation)
nodes.statement: If $M$ is an $\bF$-represented frame matroid, then there is a generator matrix $A$ of $M$ having a graph representation and at most $r(M) + 1$ rows.
assumptions: If $M$ is an $\bF$-represented frame matroid
conclusions: then there is a generator matrix $A$ of $M$ having a graph representation and at most $r(M) + 1$ rows.

nodes.name: Proposition 2.2 (balanced cycles and dense subgraphs are dependent)
nodes.statement: If $(G,\Sigma)$ is a graph representation of an $\bF$-frame matrix $A$ and $C$ is a balanced cycle of $(G,\Sigma)$ or a connected subgraph of $G$ of minimum degree 2 which is not a cycle of $G$, then $C$ is dependent in $M(A)$.
nodes.statement_short: Balanced cycles, and connected minimum-degree-2 subgraphs that are not cycles, are dependent in the represented frame matroid.
assumptions: If $(G,\Sigma)$ is a graph representation of an $\bF$-frame matrix $A$
$C$ is a balanced cycle of $(G,\Sigma)$ or a connected subgraph of $G$ of minimum degree 2 which is not a cycle of $G$
conclusions: then $C$ is dependent in $M(A)$.

nodes.name: Lemma 2.3 (graph of a 3-connected frame matroid is connected)
nodes.statement: Let $(G,\Sigma)$ be a graph representation of an $\bF$-represented frame matroid $M$. If $M$ is vertically 3-connected and has no loops, then $G$ is connected.
assumptions: Let $(G,\Sigma)$ be a graph representation of an $\bF$-represented frame matroid $M$.
If $M$ is vertically 3-connected and has no loops
conclusions: then $G$ is connected.

nodes.name: Corollary 2.4 (connected graph representation exists)
nodes.statement: Let $M$ be an $\bF$-represented frame matroid. If $M$ is vertically 3-connected, then $M$ has a graph representation $(G,\Sigma)$ with $G$ connected.
assumptions: Let $M$ be an $\bF$-represented frame matroid.
If $M$ is vertically 3-connected
conclusions: then $M$ has a graph representation $(G,\Sigma)$ with $G$ connected.

nodes.name: Lemma 3.1 (reduction to vertically $t$-connected matroids)
nodes.statement: If $t \in \bZ$ and $\cM$ is an asymptotically good minor-closed class of matroids, then the class of vertically $t$-connected matroids in $\cM$ is asymptotically good.
nodes.statement_short: Asymptotic goodness of a minor-closed class is inherited by its vertically $t$-connected members, for every fixed $t$.
assumptions: If $t \in \bZ$ and $\cM$ is an asymptotically good minor-closed class of matroids
conclusions: then the class of vertically $t$-connected matroids in $\cM$ is asymptotically good.

nodes.name: Lemma 4.1 (perturbation preserves connectivity)
nodes.statement: Let $M, N$ be $\bF$-represented matroids with $\dist(M,N) \leq k$. If $M$ is vertically $t$-connected, then $N$ is vertically $(t - 2k)$-connected.
assumptions: Let $M, N$ be $\bF$-represented matroids with $\dist(M,N) \leq k$.
If $M$ is vertically $t$-connected
conclusions: then $N$ is vertically $(t - 2k)$-connected.

nodes.name: Lemma 5.1 (Moore bound for irregular graphs)
nodes.statement: If $G$ is a graph with girth $g$ and average degree $\delta > 2$, then $g \le 4 + \tfrac{\log(|V(G)|)}{\log(\delta - 1)}$.
nodes.statement_short: Graphs of average degree above $2$ have girth at most logarithmic in the number of vertices.
nodes.origin_citation: Alon, Hoory & Linial 2001; corollary observed by Kashyap 2008
assumptions: If $G$ is a graph with girth $g$ and average degree $\delta > 2$
conclusions: then $g \le 4 + \tfrac{\log(|V(G)|)}{\log(\delta - 1)}$.

nodes.name: Lemma 5.2 (many short edge-disjoint cycles)
nodes.statement: Let $t \in \bZ^+$ and $\beta \in \bR^+$. If $G$ is a graph with $|V(G)| = n\ge \max\left(\left(\frac{4t}{\beta\log(1+\beta)}\right)^2,(1+\beta)e^4\right)$ and $|E(G)| \ge (1+\beta)n$, then $G$ has a collection of $t$ pairwise edge-disjoint cycles, each of size at most $\tfrac{2\log n}{\log(1+\beta)}$.
nodes.statement_short: A sufficiently large graph with $(1+\beta)n$ edges contains $t$ edge-disjoint cycles of logarithmic length.
assumptions: Let $t \in \bZ^+$ and $\beta \in \bR^+$.
If $G$ is a graph with $|V(G)| = n\ge \max\left(\left(\frac{4t}{\beta\log(1+\beta)}\right)^2,(1+\beta)e^4\right)$ and $|E(G)| \ge (1+\beta)n$
conclusions: then $G$ has a collection of $t$ pairwise edge-disjoint cycles, each of size at most $\tfrac{2\log n}{\log(1+\beta)}$.

nodes.name: Corollary 5.3 (rank deficiency in frame matroids)
nodes.statement: Let $\bF$ be a finite field of order $q$, let $\beta \in \bR^+$ and $t \in \bZ^+$. Let $M$ be an $\bF$-represented frame matroid with graph representation $(G,\Sigma)$, such that $G$ is connected. If $M$ satisfies \[r(M) \ge \max\left(|\bF|,(2q-3)\beta^{-1}+1-q,\tfrac{1}{q-1}\left(\tfrac{4t}{\beta\log(1+\beta)}\right)^2,\tfrac{1+\beta}{q-1}e^4\right)\] and $|M| \ge (1+q\beta)r(M)$, then there is a set $X \subseteq E(M)$ such that $r_M(X) \le |X|-t$ and $|X| \le \tfrac{4 t\log r(M)}{\log(1+\beta)}$.
nodes.statement_short: A connected frame matroid with enough elements relative to its rank has a logarithmically small set whose rank falls short of its size by $t$.
assumptions: Let $\bF$ be a finite field of order $q$, let $\beta \in \bR^+$ and $t \in \bZ^+$.
Let $M$ be an $\bF$-represented frame matroid with graph representation $(G,\Sigma)$, such that $G$ is connected.
If $M$ satisfies \[r(M) \ge \max\left(|\bF|,(2q-3)\beta^{-1}+1-q,\tfrac{1}{q-1}\left(\tfrac{4t}{\beta\log(1+\beta)}\right)^2,\tfrac{1+\beta}{q-1}e^4\right)\] and $|M| \ge (1+q\beta)r(M)$
conclusions: then there is a set $X \subseteq E(M)$ such that $r_M(X) \le |X|-t$ and $|X| \le \tfrac{4 t\log r(M)}{\log(1+\beta)}$.

nodes.name: Lemma 5.4 (logarithmic girth near a frame matroid)
nodes.statement: Let $k \in \bZ^+$, $\beta \in \bR^+$, and $\bF$ be a finite field. There exists $c \in \bZ$ such that if $M$ is a rank-$r$ $\bF$-represented matroid with $r > 2$ and $|M| \ge (1+ \beta)r$ and there is an $\bF$-represented, connected frame matroid $N$ satisfying $\dist(M,N) \le k$, then $g(M) \le c \log r$.
nodes.statement_short: A dense matroid within bounded perturbation distance of a connected frame matroid has girth $O(\log r)$.
assumptions: Let $k \in \bZ^+$, $\beta \in \bR^+$, and $\bF$ be a finite field.
if $M$ is a rank-$r$ $\bF$-represented matroid with $r > 2$ and $|M| \ge (1+ \beta)r$ and there is an $\bF$-represented, connected frame matroid $N$ satisfying $\dist(M,N) \le k$
conclusions: There exists $c \in \bZ$ such that ... $g(M) \le c \log r$.

nodes.name: Lemma 5.5 (bounded girth near the dual of a frame matroid)
nodes.statement: Let $k \in \bZ^+$, $\beta \in \bR^+$, and $\bF$ be a finite field. There exists $c \in \bZ$ so that, if $M$ is a nonempty $\bF$-represented matroid such that $|M| \ge (1+\beta) r(M)$ and there is an $\bF$-represented frame matroid $N$ with $\dist(M^*,N) \le k$ and connected graph, then $g(M) \le c$.
nodes.statement_short: A dense matroid whose dual is a bounded perturbation of a connected frame matroid has girth bounded by a constant.
assumptions: Let $k \in \bZ^+$, $\beta \in \bR^+$, and $\bF$ be a finite field.
if $M$ is a nonempty $\bF$-represented matroid such that $|M| \ge (1+\beta) r(M)$ and there is an $\bF$-represented frame matroid $N$ with $\dist(M^*,N) \le k$ and connected graph
conclusions: There exists $c \in \bZ$ so that ... $g(M) \le c$.

nodes.name: Code-to-matroid correspondence for size and rank
nodes.statement: If $C$ is a $q$-ary $[n,k,d]$ code, then $M = (\{1,\ldots, n\}, C)$ is a matroid with $|M| = n$ and $r(M) = k$. The rank function simply gives the dimension of this code and of all its puncturings.
nodes.statement_short: A $[n,k,d]$ code viewed as a represented matroid has size $n$, rank $k$, and rank function recording dimensions of punctured codes.
assumptions: If $C$ is a $q$-ary $[n,k,d]$ code
conclusions: then $M = (\{1,\ldots, n\}, C)$ is a matroid with $|M| = n$ and $r(M) = k$.

nodes.name: Minimum distance equals cogirth
nodes.statement: If $C$ is a $q$-ary $[n,k,d]$ code, then $M = (\{1,\ldots, n\}, C)$ is a matroid with $g(M^*) = d$. For that reason we sometimes write $d(M)$ for $g(M^*)$.
assumptions: If $C$ is a $q$-ary $[n,k,d]$ code
conclusions: then $M = (\{1,\ldots, n\}, C)$ is a matroid with $g(M^*) = d$.

nodes.name: Resigning preserves balanced cycles
nodes.statement: It is easily checked that $(G, \Sigma)$ and $(G, \Sigma')$ have the same collection of balanced cycles. In the representation this corresponds to scaling the rows indexed by $W$ by a factor $\gamma$.
assumptions: $(G, \Sigma')$ was obtained from $(G, \Sigma)$ by \emph{resigning}
conclusions: $(G, \Sigma)$ and $(G, \Sigma')$ have the same collection of balanced cycles.

nodes.name: Every pair of elements of a vertically 3-connected matroid lies in a circuit
nodes.statement: It is easy to show that a vertically $3$-connected matroid, with no elements $e$ such that $r_M(e) = 0$, has the property that every pair of elements is in a circuit.
assumptions: a vertically $3$-connected matroid, with no elements $e$ such that $r_M(e) = 0$
conclusions: has the property that every pair of elements is in a circuit

nodes.name: Claim 3.2 (late terms of the sequence are vertically $t$-connected)
nodes.statement: For each $n \in \bZ$ with $n \ge 2\beta^{-1}m$, the matroid $M_n$ is vertically $t$-connected.
assumptions: For each $n \in \bZ$ with $n \ge 2\beta^{-1}m$
conclusions: the matroid $M_n$ is vertically $t$-connected.

nodes.name: Perturbation distance is always finite
nodes.statement: (It is clear that any matroid on $E$ can be transformed into the rank-$0$ matroid on $E$ by a finite sequence of projections, so this distance is always finite.)
assumptions: any matroid on $E$
conclusions: this distance is always finite

nodes.name: Common extension realising bounded perturbation distance
nodes.statement: It is easy to see that, if $\dist(M_1,M_2) \le k$, then there is a matroid $M$ with ground set $E \cup C \cup D$ satisfying $M \del D \con C = M_1$ and $M \con D \del C = M_2$, where $|C|+|D| \le k$. Each elementary lift and projection can change the rank of a subset by at most one.
nodes.statement_short: Bounded perturbation distance is witnessed by a single matroid on $E \cup C \cup D$ with $|C|+|D| \le k$, and each elementary step shifts subset ranks by at most one.
assumptions: if $\dist(M_1,M_2) \le k$
conclusions: then there is a matroid $M$ with ground set $E \cup C \cup D$ satisfying $M \del D \con C = M_1$ and $M \con D \del C = M_2$, where $|C|+|D| \le k$.
Each elementary lift and projection can change the rank of a subset by at most one.

nodes.name: Geelen-Gerards-Whittle conjecture on asymptotically good minor-closed classes of codes
nodes.statement: In other words, the only asymptotically good classes of $\bF$-linear codes that are closed under puncturings and shortenings are those that contain all linear codes over some field. This result was conjectured by Geelen, Gerards, and Whittle [\ref{ggw}].
nodes.statement_short: Conjecture (GGW): the only puncturing/shortening-closed asymptotically good classes of $\bF$-linear codes are those containing all linear codes over some field.
assumptions: classes of $\bF$-linear codes that are closed under puncturings and shortenings
conclusions: the only asymptotically good [such classes] are those that contain all linear codes over some field

nodes.name: Random codes give asymptotic goodness; main result is a converse
nodes.statement: For every finite field $\bF$, the class of linear codes over $\bF$ is asymptotically good, as suitable random codes have nonvanishing rate and minimum distance. Our main result can be seen as a converse to this statement.

nodes.name: Generalisation of Kashyap's results in the binary case
nodes.statement: When $|\bF| = 2$, this substantially generalises results of Kashyap [\ref{kashyap}] which show that the classes of graphic binary codes, as well as a slightly larger class of `almost-graphic' codes, are not asymptotically good.

nodes.name: Contingency on the unpublished matroid minors structure theorem
nodes.statement: Our proof makes fundamental use of a deep theorem in structural matroid theory recently announced by Geelen, Gerards and Whittle. This theorem is one of many outcomes of the `matroid minors project', the result of more than a decade of work generalising Robertson and Seymour's graph minors structure theorem [\ref{rs}] to matroids representable over finite fields. While this theorem has now been stated in print [\ref{ggw}], its proof will stretch to hundreds of pages and has yet to be published. The reader should be aware of this contingency; for a more detailed discussion see [\ref{ggw}].
nodes.statement_short: The proof rests on the announced but as-yet-unpublished matroid minors structure theorem of Geelen, Gerards and Whittle.

nodes.name: Existence of graph representations and the binary parity-row trick
nodes.statement: It is clear that one frame matroid may have many graph representations, and that graph representations always exist unless $|\bF| = 2$, where a frame matrix having a column with exactly one nonzero entry has no graph representations since $\bF^{\times}-\{1\}$ is empty. However, appending a `parity' row to a binary frame matrix yields another row-equivalent frame matrix where every column has even support. Since we can remove redundant rows from an arbitrary frame matrix to still have a frame matrix and append a single row in this way in the binary case, we have the following statement, which we apply freely.
nodes.statement_short: Graph representations always exist except in the binary case, where appending a parity row repairs the obstruction.

nodes.name: Comparison of connectivity conventions
nodes.statement: For instance, $M$ is vertically 2-connected if and only if $M$ cannot be written as the direct sum of two positive-rank matroids. Note that other authors often use a more restrictive definition of ``vertically $t$-connected,'' which implies ours.

nodes.name: Range of $\alpha,\beta$ and goodness of the full class
nodes.statement: Note that $\alpha,\beta \le 1$ for any such $\alpha,\beta$. For any finite field $\bF$, the class of all $\bF$-represented matroids is such a class.

nodes.statement: The following theorem implies Theorem~\ref{main}.

nodes.name: Proof of Claim 3.2
nodes.statement: Suppose for a contradiction that $n \ge 2\beta^{-1}m$ and $M = M_n$ is not vertically $t$-connected. Let $(X_1,X_2)$ be a partition of $E(M)$ with $r_M(X_1) + r_M(X_2) = r(M) + t' - 1$ with $t' < t$ and $r_M(X_1),r_M(X_2) \ge t'$. Let $N_1 = M\con X_2$ and $N_2 = M \con X_1$. Since every cocircuit of $N_1$ or $N_2$ is a cocircuit of $M$, we have $g(M^*) \le \min(g(N_1^*),g(N_2^*)).We have \[ \beta|M| \le g(M^*) \le \min(g(N_1^*),g(N_2^*)) \le \tfrac{1}{2}(g(N_1^*) + g(N_2^*))\] and, since $|M| = |N_1| + |N_2|$, we have either $g(N_1^*) \ge 2\beta|N_1|$ or $g(N_2^*) \ge 2\beta|N_2|$. We may assume that the first case holds. Since each of $X_1$ and $X_2$ contains a cocircuit of $M$, we have $|N_i| = |X_i| \ge g(M^*) \ge \beta|M| \ge m$ for each $i \in \{1,2\}$. From this and $|M| = |N_1|+|N_2|$ we get \begin{align*} r(N_2) &\ge \tfrac{1}{4}\alpha|N_1| + \alpha|N_2|\\ &= \alpha\left(1 + \delta \right)|N_2| \end{align*} Now $|N_2| \ge m \ge m_2$ so $g(N_2^*) < \beta |N_2|$ by choice of $m_2$. nodes.statement_short: Split a low-connectivity $M_n$ into two contractions and derive a contradiction with the extremal choice of $m_1,m_2$ via rank and cogirth estimates.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5.2
nodes.statement: Let $m = |E(G)|$ and $\alpha = 2(\log(1+\beta))^{-1}$. By choice of $n$ we have $\frac{t \alpha \log n}{n} < \tfrac{t \alpha}{\sqrt{n}} < \tfrac{1}{2}\beta$. Let $\cC$ be a maximal collection of pairwise disjoint cycles of $G$ such that $|E(C)| \le \alpha \log n$ for each $C \in \cC$. Assume for a contradiction that $|\cC| < t$; let $G' = G \del \cup \cC$. We have $\tfrac{|E(G')|}{n} \ge \tfrac{m - t\alpha \log(n)}{n} \ge 1+\beta - \tfrac{t \alpha \log(n)}{n} > 1 + \tfrac{1}{2}\beta$, so the average degree $\delta'$ of $G'$ is at least $2 + \beta$. By maximality of $\cC$, the graph $G'$ has girth $g' > \alpha \log (n)$, so Lemma~\ref{moore} gives \begin{align*} \alpha \log(n) &< 4 + \frac{\log(n)}{\log(\delta'-1)} \le 4 + \frac{\log(n)}{\log(1+\beta).} \end{align*} Rearranging gives $\log(n) < 4\log(1+\beta)$, contradicting $n \ge (1+\beta)e^4$.
nodes.statement_short: Take a maximal family of short disjoint cycles; if fewer than $t$, the leftover graph is still dense, so the Moore bound contradicts its large girth.

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 5.3
nodes.statement: Let $A$ be an $\bF$-frame matrix generating $M$ and let $(G,\Sigma)$ be a graph representation of $A$. Pick a spanning tree $T$ of $G$. By repeatedly resigning, we may assume that the edges of $T$ have sign $1$. Note that $|E(T)| \geq r(M) - 1$. Let $G^+$ denote the undirected graph with vertex set $V(G) \times \bF^\times$ and edge set \begin{align*} & \{((\delta^{-}(e),\gamma),(\delta^{+}(e),\gamma)): e \in T, \gamma \in \bF\}\\ \cup & \{((\delta^-(e), 1), (\delta^+(e), \sign(e))): e \in E(G)\setminus T\}; \end{align*} that is, we take $q-1$ copies of $T$, and each directed edge $(u,v)$ not in $T$ with sign $\gamma$ connects the copy of $T$ corresponding to $1$ with the copy of $T$ corresponding to $\gamma$. It is easy to check that each cycle of $G^+$, by projection onto the first coordinate, corresponds to either a balanced cycle of $(G,\Sigma)$, or a subgraph of $G$ of minimum degree 2 that is not a cycle. It follows from Proposition~\ref{bicycledependent} that every cycle of $G^+$ is dependent in $M$. Now, \begin{align*} |E(G^+)| & = (q-1)|E(T)| + |M| - |E(T)| \geq (q-2)(r(M) - 1) + |M|\\ & \ge (q-1)(1+\beta)r(M) + \beta r(M) - (q-2)\\ & \ge (1+\beta)|V(G^+)| - (q-1)(1+\beta) + \beta r(M) - q + 2\\ & \ge (1+\beta)|V(G^+)|, \end{align*} where we use $|E(T)| \geq r(M)-1$ first, $|M| \geq (1+q\beta)r(M)$ second, $|V(G^+)| \le (q-1)(r(M)+1)$ third, and $r(M) \ge (2q-3)\beta^{-1}+1-q$ last. By our lower bounds for $n = |V(G+)| \geq (q-1)r(M)$ and Lemma~\ref{disjointcircuits}, the graph $G^+$ contains $t$ pairwise disjoint cycles, each of size at most $\frac{2\log n}{\log(1+\beta)} \le \frac{4 \log r(M)}{\log(1+\beta)}$. Each of these cycles of $G$ is dependent in $M$, and it is thus easy to see that their union satisfies the result.
nodes.statement_short: Build the $(q-1)$-fold covering graph $G^+$ of the signed graph, whose cycles are dependent in $M$, then apply the disjoint-cycles lemma to $G^+$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5.4
nodes.statement: Let $\beta' = \tfrac{1}{2}\beta$ and $c \ge \max\Big((2q-3)\beta^{-1}+1-q$, $|\bF|$, $\left(\tfrac{4(k+1)}{\beta'\log(1+\beta')}\right)^2$, $(1+\beta')e^4\Big)+k$ be an integer so that $4(k+1)\log(x+k) \le c \log(1+\beta')\log x$ for all $x \ge c$. Since $\beta' > 0$ we know that $M$ has a circuit, so $g(M) \le r+1$. If $r \le c-1$ then $g(M) \le r+1 \le c \le c \log r$, so the result holds; we may thus assume that $r \ge c$. Let $M^+$ be a matroid and $C,D \subseteq E(M^+)$ be sets of size at most $k$ so that $M^+ \con C \del D = M$ and $M^+ \con D \del C = N$. Since each $Y \subseteq E(M)$ satisfies $r_{M^+}(Y) \ge r_M(Y) \ge r_{M^+}(Y) - r_{M^+}(C) \ge r_{M^+}(Y) - k$ and a similar statement holds for $N$, we have $|r_M(Y) - r_{N}(Y)| \le k$ for each $Y \subseteq E(M)$. In particular, $r+k \ge r(N) \ge r - k \ge c-k$. By choice of $c$, Corollary~\ref{framematroidrankdeficiency} implies there is a set $X \subseteq E(N)$ with $r_{N}(X) \le |X|-(k+1)$ and $|X| \le \frac{4(k+1)\log(r(N))}{\log(1+\beta')} \le \tfrac{4(k+1)\log(r+k)}{\log(1+\beta')} \le c \log r$. Now $r_M(X) \le r_{N}(X) + k < |X|$, so $X$ contains a circuit of $M$ and therefore $g(M) \le c \log r$, as required.
nodes.statement_short: Transfer a rank-deficient logarithmic-size set from the nearby frame matroid $N$ to $M$, using that perturbation shifts ranks by at most $k$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5.5
nodes.statement: We may assume that $\beta \le 1$. Let $c = \lceil 12 \beta^{-1}(3k+1) \rceil$. If $|M| \le c$ then the result clearly holds, so we will assume otherwise. Let $M^+$ be a matroid and $C,D \subseteq E(M^+)$ be sets of size at most $k$ so that $M^+ \con C \del D = M^*$ and $M^+ \con D \del C = N$. As before, we have $|r_{M^*}(Y)-r_N(Y)| \le k$ for each $Y \subseteq E(M^*)$. Let $A$ be an $\bF$-frame matrix generating $N$ with $r(N)$ rows (or $r(N)+1$ rows if $|\bF| = 2$), and $(G,\Sigma)$ be an $\bF^{\times}$-labelled graph associated with $N$. We have $|M^*| = |M| \ge (1+\beta)r(M) = (1+\beta)(|M^*| - r(M^*))$, giving $|M^*| \le (1 + \beta^{-1})r(M^*) \le 2\beta^{-1}r(M^*)$. Now $k \le r(M^*)-k \le r(N) \le |V(G)|+1 \le 2|V(G)|$, so \[|E(G)| = |N| = |M^*| \le 2\beta^{-1}(|V(G)|+k) \le 6\beta^{-1}|V(G)|.\] Therefore $G$ has average degree at most $12\beta^{-1}$. If $|V(G)| < 2(k+1)$, then $2(k+1)-1 \ge r(N) \ge r(M^*)-k$ so $r(M^*) \le 3k+1$. This gives $|M^*| \le 2\beta^{-1}(3k+1) < c$, a contradiction. Therefore $|V(G)| \ge 2(k+1)$, so there is a collection of $2(k+1)$ vertices of $G$ whose degrees sum to at most $12\beta^{-1}(k+1)$, so there is a set $F \subseteq E(G)$ such that $|F| \le 12\beta^{-1}(k+1) \le c$ and $r(N \del F) \le r(N)+1 - 2(k+1)$ (since $A$ has at most $r(N)+1$ rows and $A[E(N)-F]$ has at least $2(k+1)$ zero rows). Now \[r(M^* \del F) \le r(N \del F) + k \le r(N) - 2k -1 +k \le r(M^*) -1.\] Thus $F$ contains a cocircuit of $M^*$, which is a circuit of $M$, giving $g(M) \le c$.
nodes.statement_short: Bound the average degree of the frame matroid's graph, pick low-degree vertices to isolate a small edge set $F$ that drops the rank, so $F$ contains a circuit of $M$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 6.1
nodes.statement: If $\cM$ contains all projective geometries over $\Fprime$, then $\cM$ contains all $\Fprime$-represented matroids so is clearly asymptotically good. Suppose that $\cM$ does not contain all projective geometries over $\Fprime$ but is asymptotically good. By Theorem~\ref{big}, there is an integer $k$ so that every vertically $k$-connected matroid $M \in \cM$ satisfies $\dist(M,N) \le k$ or $\dist(M^*,N) \le k$ for some $\bF$-represented frame matroid $N$; moreover, $N$ is vertically $3$-connected by Lemma \ref{lem:connectedperturb}, so by Corollary \ref{cor:graphconn} we may assume the associated graph is connected. Let $\cM_k$ denote the class of vertically $(2k+3)$-connected matroids in $M$. Note that every such matroid is also vertically $k$-connected. By Lemma~\ref{connreduction}, the class $\cM_k$ is asymptotically good, so $\cM_k$ contains an $(\alpha,\alpha)$-good sequence for some $\alpha \in (0,1)$. Let $\beta = (1-\alpha)^{-1}-1$ and let $c$ be the maximum of the two integers given by Lemmas~\ref{nearframe} and~\ref{nearcoframe} for $\bF$, $\beta$ and $k$. Let $n_0$ be an integer so that $c \log n < \alpha n$ for all $n \ge n_0$. There is a matroid $M \in \cM_k$ so that $|M| \ge n_0$, $d(M) = g(M^*) \ge \alpha|M|$ and $r(M) \ge \alpha|M|$. The last inequality gives $|M^*| \ge (1+\beta)r(M^*)$, so by Lemma~\ref{nearframe} or~\ref{nearcoframe} we have $d(M) \le c \log r(M^*) \le c \log |M^*| < \alpha |M^*|$, a contradiction.
nodes.statement_short: Easy direction is immediate; for the converse, combine the structure theorem with the connectivity reduction and the girth bounds to contradict asymptotic goodness.

nodes.name: Define the parameter sets $A_\beta$ and $B$ and their suprema
nodes.statement: For each $\beta \in \bR^+$ let $A_{\beta}$ denote the set of all $\alpha \in \bR^+$ such that $\cM$ contains an $(\alpha,\beta)$-good sequence. Let $B = \{\beta \in \bR^+: A_\beta \ne \varnothing\}$. By assumption, $B$ is a nonempty interval with $\inf(B) = 0$ and $\sup(B) \le 1$; let $\beta_{\max} = \sup(B)$. Each nonempty $A_x$ is also such an interval; for each $x \in B$, let $\alpha_{\max}(x) = \sup(A_x)$, noting that $\alpha_{\max}(x) \le 1$.
nodes.statement_short: Set up the sets of achievable rate/distance parameters and their extremal values $\beta_{\max}$, $\alpha_{\max}(x)$.

nodes.name: Choose $\beta$, $\delta$, $\alpha$ and a good sequence
nodes.statement: Let $\beta \in (\tfrac{2}{3}\beta_{\max},\beta_{\max})$ and let $\delta = \tfrac{\beta}{4(1-\beta)}$. Set $\alpha_{\max} = \alpha_{\max}(\beta)$ and let $\alpha \in ((1+\tfrac{1}{2}\delta)^{-1}\alpha_{\max},\alpha_{\max})$. We have $\beta \in B$ and $\alpha \in A_{\beta}$; let $M_0, M_1, \dotsc$ be an $(\alpha,\beta)$-good sequence of matroids in $\cM$.
nodes.statement_short: Pick near-extremal parameters and fix an $(\alpha,\beta)$-good sequence in $\cM$.

nodes.name: Extract the thresholds $m_1, m_2$ and set $m$
nodes.statement:
Since $2 eta >  eta_{\max}$ we have $2 eta 
otin B$ so $A_{2 eta} = \varnothing$ and in particular $	frac{1}{2}\alpha 
otin A_{2 eta}$. Moreover, we have $(1+\delta)\alpha > \alpha_{\max}$ so $(1+\delta)\alpha 
otin A_ eta$. There are therefore integers $m_1$ and $m_2$ such that and every matroid $M \in \cM$ with $|M| \ge m_1$ satisfies $g(M^*) < 2 eta |M|$ or $r(M) < 	frac{1}{2}\alpha|M|$, and every matroid $M \in \cM$ with $|M| \ge m_2$ satisfies $g(M^*) <  eta |M|$ or $r(M) < \alpha(1+\delta)|M|$. nodes.name: Conclude from the claim
nodes.statement: By the claim, all but finitely many terms of the sequence $M_0,M_1, \dotsc$ are vertically $t$-connected, so the class of vertically $t$-connected matroids in $\cM$ is asymptotically good, as required.
nodes.statement_short: Cofinitely many terms are vertically $t$-connected, which gives the asymptotic goodness of the connected subclass.

nodes.name: Assume $M_n$ is not vertically $t$-connected and fix a violating partition
nodes.statement: Suppose for a contradiction that $n \ge 2\beta^{-1}m$ and $M = M_n$ is not vertically $t$-connected. Let $(X_1,X_2)$ be a partition of $E(M)$ with $r_M(X_1) + r_M(X_2) = r(M) + t' - 1$ with $t' < t$ and $r_M(X_1),r_M(X_2) \ge t'$.
nodes.statement_short: Set up the contradiction with a low-rank partition witnessing failure of vertical $t$-connectivity.

nodes.name: Form the contractions $N_1, N_2$ and bound their ranks
nodes.statement: Let $N_1 = M\con X_2$ and $N_2 = M \con X_1$. Note that $N_1,N_2 \in \cM$ and that $r(N_i) = r(M)-r_M(X_{3-i}) > r(M)-t+1$, so $r(N_1) + r(N_2) > r(M)-2t$.
nodes.statement_short: Introduce the two contractions and note their ranks nearly add up to $r(M)$.

nodes.name: Cogirth averaging and choice of the good side
nodes.statement: Since every cocircuit of $N_1$ or $N_2$ is a cocircuit of $M$, we have $g(M^*) \le \min(g(N_1^*),g(N_2^*)).We have \[ \beta|M| \le g(M^*) \le \min(g(N_1^*),g(N_2^*)) \le \tfrac{1}{2}(g(N_1^*) + g(N_2^*))\] and, since $|M| = |N_1| + |N_2|$, we have either $g(N_1^*) \ge 2\beta|N_1|$ or $g(N_2^*) \ge 2\beta|N_2|$. We may assume that the first case holds.
nodes.statement_short: One of the two parts has cogirth at least $2\beta$ times its size; assume it is $N_1$.

nodes.name: Size lower bounds and rank bound for $N_1$
nodes.statement: Since each of $X_1$ and $X_2$ contains a cocircuit of $M$, we have $|N_i| = |X_i| \ge g(M^*) \ge \beta|M| \ge m$ for each $i \in \{1,2\}$. Since $|N_1| + |N_2| = |M|$, this implies that $|N_1| \ge \tfrac{\beta}{1-\beta}|N_2|$. Moreover, $m \ge m_1$ gives $r(N_1) < \tfrac{1}{2}\alpha|N_1|$.
nodes.statement_short: Both parts are large, so the $m_1$ threshold forces $N_1$ to have small rank.

nodes.name: Rank chain forcing $r(N_2) \ge \alpha(1+\delta)|N_2|$
nodes.statement: We have \begin{align*} \alpha|M| &\le r(M) \\ &< r(N_1) + r(N_2) + 2t\\ &< \tfrac{1}{2}\alpha|N_1| + r(N_2) + 2t\\ &\le \tfrac{3}{4}\alpha|N_1| + r(N_2), \end{align*} Where the last line uses $\tfrac{1}{4}\alpha|N_1| \ge \tfrac{1}{4}\alpha m \ge 2t$. From this and $|M| = |N_1|+|N_2|$ we get \begin{align*} r(N_2) &\ge \tfrac{1}{4}\alpha|N_1| + \alpha|N_2|\\ &= \alpha\left(1 + \delta \right)|N_2| \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Chain the rank inequalities to show $N_2$ has rate at least $\alpha(1+\delta)$.

nodes.name: Contradiction via the $m_2$ threshold
nodes.statement: Now $|N_2| \ge m \ge m_2$ so $g(N_2^*) < \beta |N_2|$ by choice of $m_2$. However $g(M^*) \le g(N_2^*)$ and $\beta|N_2| < \beta|M|$, so $g(M^*) < \beta|M|$, contradicting the definition of $M$.
nodes.statement_short: The $m_2$ threshold makes $N_2$'s cogirth too small, contradicting the goodness of $M$.

nodes.name: Set $m$, $\alpha$ and record the numerical inequality
nodes.statement: Let $m = |E(G)|$ and $\alpha = 2(\log(1+\beta))^{-1}$. By choice of $n$ we have $\frac{t \alpha \log n}{n} < \tfrac{t \alpha}{\sqrt{n}} < \tfrac{1}{2}\beta$.
nodes.statement_short: Introduce the cycle-length parameter $\alpha$ and note the hypothesis makes $t\alpha\log n / n$ small.

nodes.name: Maximal family of short disjoint cycles and the contradiction hypothesis
nodes.statement: Let $\cC$ be a maximal collection of pairwise disjoint cycles of $G$ such that $|E(C)| \le \alpha \log n$ for each $C \in \cC$. Assume for a contradiction that $|\cC| < t$; let $G' = G \del \cup \cC$.
nodes.statement_short: Choose a maximal short disjoint cycle family and suppose it has fewer than $t$ members.

nodes.name: The leftover graph still has average degree above $2$
nodes.statement: We have $\tfrac{|E(G')|}{n} \ge \tfrac{m - t\alpha \log(n)}{n} \ge 1+\beta - \tfrac{t \alpha \log(n)}{n} > 1 + \tfrac{1}{2}\beta$, so the average degree $\delta'$ of $G'$ is at least $2 + \beta$.
nodes.statement_short: Deleting the few short cycles leaves enough edges that $G'$ has average degree $\ge 2+\beta$.

nodes.name: Apply the Moore bound to $G'$
nodes.statement: By maximality of $\cC$, the graph $G'$ has girth $g' > \alpha \log (n)$, so Lemma~\ref{moore} gives \begin{align*} \alpha \log(n) &< 4 + \frac{\log(n)}{\log(\delta'-1)} \le 4 + \frac{\log(n)}{\log(1+\beta).} \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Maximality forces large girth in $G'$, so the Moore bound applies.

nodes.name: Rearrange to contradict the lower bound on $n$
nodes.statement: Rearranging gives $\log(n) < 4\log(1+\beta)$, contradicting $n \ge (1+\beta)e^4$.
nodes.statement_short: The resulting inequality contradicts the assumed lower bound on $n$.

nodes.name: Normalise a graph representation by resigning a spanning tree
nodes.statement: Let $A$ be an $\bF$-frame matrix generating $M$ and let $(G,\Sigma)$ be a graph representation of $A$. Pick a spanning tree $T$ of $G$. By repeatedly resigning, we may assume that the edges of $T$ have sign $1$. Note that $|E(T)| \geq r(M) - 1$.
nodes.statement_short: Resign so that a spanning tree of the representing graph has all signs $1$.

nodes.name: Construct the covering graph $G^+$
nodes.statement: Let $G^+$ denote the undirected graph with vertex set $V(G) \times \bF^\times$ and edge set \begin{align*} & \{((\delta^{-}(e),\gamma),(\delta^{+}(e),\gamma)): e \in T, \gamma \in \bF\}\\ \cup & \{((\delta^-(e), 1), (\delta^+(e), \sign(e))): e \in E(G)\setminus T\}; \end{align*} that is, we take $q-1$ copies of $T$, and each directed edge $(u,v)$ not in $T$ with sign $\gamma$ connects the copy of $T$ corresponding to $1$ with the copy of $T$ corresponding to $\gamma$.
nodes.statement_short: Build the $(q-1)$-fold cover $G^+$: copies of the tree glued along non-tree edges according to their signs.

nodes.name: Cycles of $G^+$ are dependent in $M$
nodes.statement: It is easy to check that each cycle of $G^+$, by projection onto the first coordinate, corresponds to either a balanced cycle of $(G,\Sigma)$, or a subgraph of $G$ of minimum degree 2 that is not a cycle. It follows from Proposition~\ref{bicycledependent} that every cycle of $G^+$ is dependent in $M$.
nodes.statement_short: Project cycles of $G^+$ down and invoke the dependence proposition.

nodes.name: Edge count of $G^+$ exceeds $(1+\beta)|V(G^+)|$
nodes.statement: Now, \begin{align*} |E(G^+)| & = (q-1)|E(T)| + |M| - |E(T)| \geq (q-2)(r(M) - 1) + |M|\\ & \ge (q-1)(1+\beta)r(M) + \beta r(M) - (q-2)\\ & \ge (1+\beta)|V(G^+)| - (q-1)(1+\beta) + \beta r(M) - q + 2\\ & \ge (1+\beta)|V(G^+)|, \end{align*} where we use $|E(T)| \geq r(M)-1$ first, $|M| \geq (1+q\beta)r(M)$ second, $|V(G^+)| \le (q-1)(r(M)+1)$ third, and $r(M) \ge (2q-3)\beta^{-1}+1-q$ last.
nodes.statement_short: Verify the density hypothesis $|E(G^+)| \ge (1+\beta)|V(G^+)|$ for the cover.

nodes.name: Extract $t$ disjoint short cycles and take their union
nodes.statement: By our lower bounds for $n = |V(G+)| \geq (q-1)r(M)$ and Lemma~\ref{disjointcircuits}, the graph $G^+$ contains $t$ pairwise disjoint cycles, each of size at most $\frac{2\log n}{\log(1+\beta)} \le \frac{4 \log r(M)}{\log(1+\beta)}$. Each of these cycles of $G$ is dependent in $M$, and it is thus easy to see that their union satisfies the result.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the disjoint-cycles lemma to $G^+$; the union of the $t$ dependent cycles is the required rank-deficient set.

nodes.name: Choose $\beta'$ and the constant $c$
nodes.statement: Let $\beta' = \tfrac{1}{2}\beta$ and $c \ge \max\Big((2q-3)\beta^{-1}+1-q$, $|\bF|$, $\left(\tfrac{4(k+1)}{\beta'\log(1+\beta')}\right)^2$, $(1+\beta')e^4\Big)+k$ be an integer so that $4(k+1)\log(x+k) \le c \log(1+\beta')\log x$ for all $x \ge c$.
nodes.statement_short: Fix the constant $c$ large enough for the later application of the rank-deficiency corollary.

nodes.name: Dispose of small rank
nodes.statement: Since $\beta' > 0$ we know that $M$ has a circuit, so $g(M) \le r+1$. If $r \le c-1$ then $g(M) \le r+1 \le c \le c \log r$, so the result holds; we may thus assume that $r \ge c$.
nodes.statement_short: Handle $r \le c-1$ trivially, so assume $r \ge c$.

nodes.name: Realise the perturbation by a common extension $M^+$
nodes.statement: Let $M^+$ be a matroid and $C,D \subseteq E(M^+)$ be sets of size at most $k$ so that $M^+ \con C \del D = M$ and $M^+ \con D \del C = N$.
nodes.statement_short: Introduce the single matroid $M^+$ witnessing $\dist(M,N) \le k$.

nodes.name: Rank functions of $M$ and $N$ differ by at most $k$
nodes.statement: Since each $Y \subseteq E(M)$ satisfies $r_{M^+}(Y) \ge r_M(Y) \ge r_{M^+}(Y) - r_{M^+}(C) \ge r_{M^+}(Y) - k$ and a similar statement holds for $N$, we have $|r_M(Y) - r_{N}(Y)| \le k$ for each $Y \subseteq E(M)$. In particular, $r+k \ge r(N) \ge r - k \ge c-k$.
nodes.statement_short: Bound the rank discrepancy between $M$ and $N$ by $k$, and hence bound $r(N)$.

nodes.name: Apply the frame-matroid rank-deficiency corollary to $N$
nodes.statement: By choice of $c$, Corollary~\ref{framematroidrankdeficiency} implies there is a set $X \subseteq E(N)$ with $r_{N}(X) \le |X|-(k+1)$ and $|X| \le \frac{4(k+1)\log(r(N))}{\log(1+\beta')} \le \tfrac{4(k+1)\log(r+k)}{\log(1+\beta')} \le c \log r$.
nodes.statement_short: Get from the corollary a logarithmically small set $X$ in $N$ with rank deficiency $k+1$.

nodes.name: Transfer $X$ back to $M$ to bound the girth
nodes.statement: Now $r_M(X) \le r_{N}(X) + k < |X|$, so $X$ contains a circuit of $M$ and therefore $g(M) \le c \log r$, as required.
nodes.statement_short: $X$ stays dependent in $M$, giving the logarithmic girth bound.

nodes.name: Normalise $\beta$, define $c$ and dispose of small $|M|$
nodes.statement: We may assume that $\beta \le 1$. Let $c = \lceil 12 \beta^{-1}(3k+1) \rceil$. If $|M| \le c$ then the result clearly holds, so we will assume otherwise.
nodes.statement_short: Fix the constant $c$ and reduce to the case $|M| > c$.

nodes.name: Common extension $M^+$ and a frame representation of $N$
nodes.statement: Let $M^+$ be a matroid and $C,D \subseteq E(M^+)$ be sets of size at most $k$ so that $M^+ \con C \del D = M^*$ and $M^+ \con D \del C = N$. As before, we have $|r_{M^*}(Y)-r_N(Y)| \le k$ for each $Y \subseteq E(M^*)$. Let $A$ be an $\bF$-frame matrix generating $N$ with $r(N)$ rows (or $r(N)+1$ rows if $|\bF| = 2$), and $(G,\Sigma)$ be an $\bF^{\times}$-labelled graph associated with $N$.
nodes.statement_short: Realise $\dist(M^*,N) \le k$ by $M^+$ and fix a low-row frame representation $(G,\Sigma)$ of $N$.

nodes.name: Bound $|M^*|$ in terms of $r(M^*)$
nodes.statement: We have $|M^*| = |M| \ge (1+\beta)r(M) = (1+\beta)(|M^*| - r(M^*))$, giving $|M^*| \le (1 + \beta^{-1})r(M^*) \le 2\beta^{-1}r(M^*)$.
nodes.statement_short: Density of $M$ translates into $|M^*| \le 2\beta^{-1} r(M^*)$.

nodes.name: The representing graph has bounded average degree
nodes.statement: Now $k \le r(M^*)-k \le r(N) \le |V(G)|+1 \le 2|V(G)|$, so \[|E(G)| = |N| = |M^*| \le 2\beta^{-1}(|V(G)|+k) \le 6\beta^{-1}|V(G)|.\] Therefore $G$ has average degree at most $12\beta^{-1}$.
nodes.statement_short: Convert the size bound into an average-degree bound of $12\beta^{-1}$ for $G$.

nodes.name: Rule out few vertices
nodes.statement: If $|V(G)| < 2(k+1)$, then $2(k+1)-1 \ge r(N) \ge r(M^*)-k$ so $r(M^*) \le 3k+1$. This gives $|M^*| \le 2\beta^{-1}(3k+1) < c$, a contradiction.
nodes.statement_short: The case $|V(G)| < 2(k+1)$ contradicts $|M| > c$.

nodes.name: Select a small edge set $F$ around low-degree vertices
nodes.statement: Therefore $|V(G)| \ge 2(k+1)$, so there is a collection of $2(k+1)$ vertices of $G$ whose degrees sum to at most $12\beta^{-1}(k+1)$, so there is a set $F \subseteq E(G)$ such that $|F| \le 12\beta^{-1}(k+1) \le c$ and $r(N \del F) \le r(N)+1 - 2(k+1)$ (since $A$ has at most $r(N)+1$ rows and $A[E(N)-F]$ has at least $2(k+1)$ zero rows).
nodes.statement_short: Average-degree counting gives a bounded edge set $F$ whose deletion drops $r(N)$ by $2(k+1)-1$.

nodes.name: $F$ contains a cocircuit of $M^*$, hence a circuit of $M$
nodes.statement: Now \[r(M^* \del F) \le r(N \del F) + k \le r(N) - 2k -1 +k \le r(M^*) -1.\] Thus $F$ contains a cocircuit of $M^*$, which is a circuit of $M$, giving $g(M) \le c$.
nodes.statement_short: Deleting $F$ drops the rank of $M^*$, so $F$ contains a circuit of $M$ of size at most $c$.

nodes.name: Easy direction: projective geometries give goodness
nodes.statement: If $\cM$ contains all projective geometries over $\Fprime$, then $\cM$ contains all $\Fprime$-represented matroids so is clearly asymptotically good.
nodes.statement_short: Containing all $\Fprime$-projective geometries immediately yields asymptotic goodness.

nodes.name: Apply the structure theorem and pass to $\cM_k$
nodes.statement: Suppose that $\cM$ does not contain all projective geometries over $\Fprime$ but is asymptotically good. By Theorem~\ref{big}, there is an integer $k$ so that every vertically $k$-connected matroid $M \in \cM$ satisfies $\dist(M,N) \le k$ or $\dist(M^*,N) \le k$ for some $\bF$-represented frame matroid $N$; moreover, $N$ is vertically $3$-connected by Lemma \ref{lem:connectedperturb}, so by Corollary \ref{cor:graphconn} we may assume the associated graph is connected. Let $\cM_k$ denote the class of vertically $(2k+3)$-connected matroids in $M$. Note that every such matroid is also vertically $k$-connected.
nodes.statement_short: Assume the contrary, invoke the structure theorem, and restrict to the vertically $(2k+3)$-connected subclass with connected frame representations.

nodes.name: Goodness of $\cM_k$ and choice of $c$, $n_0$
nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{connreduction}, the class $\cM_k$ is asymptotically good, so $\cM_k$ contains an $(\alpha,\alpha)$-good sequence for some $\alpha \in (0,1)$. Let $\beta = (1-\alpha)^{-1}-1$ and let $c$ be the maximum of the two integers given by Lemmas~\ref{nearframe} and~\ref{nearcoframe} for $\bF$, $\beta$ and $k$. Let $n_0$ be an integer so that $c \log n < \alpha n$ for all $n \ge n_0$.
nodes.statement_short: Use the connectivity reduction to keep goodness in $\cM_k$, then fix the girth constant $c$ and threshold $n_0$.

nodes.name: Girth bounds contradict the good sequence
nodes.statement: There is a matroid $M \in \cM_k$ so that $|M| \ge n_0$, $d(M) = g(M^*) \ge \alpha|M|$ and $r(M) \ge \alpha|M|$. The last inequality gives $|M^*| \ge (1+\beta)r(M^*)$, so by Lemma~\ref{nearframe} or~\ref{nearcoframe} we have $d(M) \le c \log r(M^*) \le c \log |M^*| < \alpha |M^*|$, a contradiction.
nodes.statement_short: A large good member of $\cM_k$ has cogirth both at least $\alpha|M|$ and at most $c\log|M^*|$ — a contradiction.
